While Theorem T4 and Section 4.3 correctly disclaim semantic consumption as out of scope, technical artifacts in literature_matrix_r4.json and formal_semantics_r4.md must be scrubbed.
blockers.required_resolution_criteria: Scrub all ambiguous 'consumption' occurrences across all Phase 0 documents. Replace with explicit, falsifiable systems terminology: 'server-attested disclosure supply', 'inference dispatch continuity', or 'dispatched projection digest'. Reaffirm that neural semantic consumption is strictly OUT OF SCOPE.

blockers.required_resolution_criteria: Embed the formal Novelty Outcome Rule in novelty_contract_r4.md, experiments_plan_r4.json, and statistical_plan_r4.md: If C3 matches C4 in decision safety (zero invalid admissions), GLHS explicitly surrenders decision-safety superiority over compact capability tokens and restricts novelty framing strictly to lifecycle state-machine governance, two-digest transport attestation, tamper-evident lineage binding, and bit-exact forensic audit reconstructability.
blockers.phase_3_audit_notes: Adversarially audited by Subagent 5. Evaluation across 15 standard schedules in test_benchmark_decision_concordance_schedule_matrix confirms C3 matches C4 in decision safety (0 decision disagreements across all clean, stale, prompt substitution, undisclosed evidence, and corrupted signature schedules). Per the Novelty Outcome Rule (novelty_contract_r4.md §6), GLHS R4 explicitly surrenders any claim of decision-safety superiority over compact capability tokens (C3) and confines its novelty claims strictly to full-lifecycle state-machine governance, server-attested two-digest dispatch receipts, tamper-evident non-downgradable proposal lineage, and bit-exact forensic audit reconstructability (reconstructability score 100 vs 75).

blockers.phase_3_audit_notes: Adversarially audited by Subagent 5. Evidence containment and temporal validity checks are fully operational. Zero strawman vulnerabilities exist.

blockers.title: Chronology Validator Non-Strict Inequality & Missing R4 Validator Harness
blockers.threat_description: The chronology validator in research/glhs_journal/q3_r3/chronology_validator.py checks 'if exec_dt < freeze_dt:', which evaluates to False when exec_dt == freeze_dt. This fails to enforce the mandatory strict inequality 'freeze_dt < exec_dt', allowing retroactive contemporaneous executions to pass. Furthermore, there is no dedicated chronology validator for R4 protocols (E15–E22).
blockers.required_resolution_criteria: Implement research/glhs_journal/q4_r4/chronology_validator_r4.py enforcing strict inequality 'if exec_dt <= freeze_dt: reject' and validating all prospective protocols E15 through E22. Patch existing R3 validator to enforce strict inequality.
